newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy sees 1st half loss, improved year.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy sees 1st half loss, improved year.

text.p: Best Buy Co Inc said Wednesday it expects comparable store sales will decline in the first half of its current fiscal 1998 year, resulting in a loss for the first six months.
However, improved earnings are expected for the fiscal year, the consumer electronics retailer said in a statement.
Best Buy said its expected first half sales decline is due to continued softness in a number of its categories and the company's decision to focus on more profitable assortments.

Best Buy also said it believes that its gross profit percentage will improve over last year due to the continued growth in sales of performance service plans, improvements in assortment planning and model transition and increased effectiveness of advertising and promotions.
Management expects some of this improvement will be offset by higher operating expenses, it added.
As previously announced, Best Buy expects to open 13 new stores and will be reporting sales on a quarterly basis instead of on a monthly basis in fiscal 1998.
The company operates 272 stores in 32 states.
Best Buy said its financial position has improved, compared with the prior year-end, as inventories are about $70 million lower, including the addition of 21 new stores.

In addition, the company said its investment in developed property declined by more than $70 million as more than $100 million was realized through the sale and leaseback of properties in fiscal 1997.

Best Buy said it ended the fiscal year with $90 million in cash, has had minimal daily bank borrowings since mid-December 1996 and is currently in compliance with all covenants in its bank working capital facility.

Earlier, Best Buy reported earnings for its fiscal 1997 year ended March 1, 1997 fell to $1.7 million or $0.04 a share from $48.0 million or $1.10 a share in fiscal 1996. Sales in fiscal 1997 rose eight percent over a year earlier to $7.77 billion.
